title: Distinguished Engineer - Systems Architecture
description:
When you join Verizon

You want more out of a career. A place to share your ideas freely — even if they’re daring or different. Where the true you can learn, grow, and thrive. At Verizon, we power and empower how people live, work and play by connecting them to what brings them joy. We do what we love — driving innovation, creativity, and impact in the world. Our V Team is a community of people who anticipate, lead, and believe that listening is where learning begins. In crisis and in celebration, we come together — lifting our communities and building trust in how we show up, everywhere & always. Want in? Join the #VTeamLife.

What you’ll be doing...


As a Distinguished Engineer- Systems Architecture part of the Enterprise Network team within the Business Product Engineering organization you will be responsible for defining network architectures and driving innovation in support of enterprise and inbuilding networks. The Distinguished Engineer will be responsible for leading the development of technologies in support of enterprise use-case solutions on private and public wireless networks (e.g., private breakout [PBO], dynamic network slicing).


You will be responsible for the following but not limited to:


  • Contributing to technology roadmapping, intellectual property ideation, and defining standardized deployment architectures across emerging focus areas.
  • Researching industry trends and work with vendors and partners to recommend network technologies and solutions that will drive business for enterprises.
  • Working across technology industry partners, network and relevant technology vendor providers, and system integrators to drive new architectures in support of products in clear alignment with product teams and direct customer engagements.
  • Leading discussions across network teams (including planning, engineering, operations) to define and align on these architectures through network project processes ensuring to meet the highest standard of quality.
  • Providing recommendations on which solutions and deployment technology architecture Verizon should pursue and build an infrastructure for testing, incubation and connectivity with internal and external partners .
  • Designing and engineering the infrastructure for trial scenarios, as well as managing the progression and development of HW and SW in alignment with product roadmaps and business product needs.
  • Translating customer requirements and challenges to technology solutions and working with leadership and across organizations in network and business to develop these solutions towards cohesive, monetizable solutions and drive continuous product innovation and revenue growth.




What we’re looking for...

The ideal candidate will have a deep technical background in end-to-end wireless architectures (4G/5G RAN and Core, Private Wireless Networks, network slicing). A strong knowledge of 3GPP standards both existing and upcoming with the ability to translate them to vendor requirements. You bring a track record of innovation—whether through defining architecture, authoring IP/patents, or operationalizing emerging capabilities.


You will possess the strategic acumen to develop key action plans, establish architectural baselines, and drive cross-functional alignment through ambiguity and fast-changing priorities. You are able to work in high-stakes deployment environments and serve as a mentor and technical authority to elevate peers and cross functional network teams. You are able to influence stakeholders and decision makers on technical recommended directions based on factual evidence from research and testing.

Travel up to 25% is expected.



You’ll need to have:


  • Bachelor's degree or four or more years of relevant work experience.
  • Eight or more years of relevant experience required, demonstrated through one or a combination of work and/or military experience, or specialized training.
  • Experience in wireless networking, network architecture, or systems integration.
  • Experience in large-scale network architecture or integration projects, 4G/5G core networks, MEC, IP routing, RF design, and edge/private network deployments.
  • Understanding of end-to-end wireless architectures, and enterprise connectivity solutions.
  • Willingness to travel up to 25% or less of the time.

Even better if you have one or more of the following:


  • Bachelor's or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical discipline.
  • Experience with Private Wireless Networks (PWN), portable/mobile network kits, or rapid-deployment network infrastructure.
  • Familiarity with Private Networks, Inbuilding network solutions, Private Breakout (PBO), network slicing.
  • Experience in building strong relationships with stakeholders, technical partners, technology vendors, and cross-functional leadership.
  • Possess excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to convey complex technical concepts to executive stakeholders.
  • Self-motivated leadership with a track record of thriving in high-ambiguity environments.
  • Proven track record of innovation, patent filings, or defining scalable, productized technical standards.
  • Possess mentoring and technical leadership skills to scale team capabilities and field operations expertise.

If Verizon and this role sound like a fit for you, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every “even better” qualification listed above.


Where you’ll be working

In this hybrid role, you'll have a defined work location that includes working from home and a minimum of three days per week in the office, which will be set by your manager. Employees are responsible for maintaining compliance with hybrid work policies.

Scheduled Weekly Hours

40

Equal Employment Opportunity

Verizon is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to veteran status, disability or other legally protected characteristics.

Benefits and Compensation

Our benefits are designed to help you move forward in your career, and in areas of your life outside of Verizon. From health and wellness benefit options including: medical, dental, vision, short and long term disability, basic life insurance, supplemental life insurance, AD&D insurance, identity theft protection, pet insurance and group home & auto insurance. We also offer a matched 401(k) savings plan, up to 8 company paid holidays per year and up to 6 personal days per year, paid parental leave, adoption assistance and tuition assistance, plus other incentives, we’ve got you covered with our award-winning total rewards package. Depending on the role, employees have the opportunity to receive compensation in the form of premium pay such as overtime, shift differential, holiday pay, allowances, etc. Newly hired employees receive up to 15 days of vacation per year, which grows with additional service. For part-timers, your coverage will vary as you may be eligible for some of these benefits depending on your individual circumstances.

Job Description:

Baker Tilly, one of the fastest growing CPA advisory firms in the nation, has an incredible career opportunity for a State & Local Tax Senior (Income Tax & Residency) to join our State & Local Tax (SALT) practice!

Our SALT practice is made up of 300+ professionals across the U.S., providing a full spectrum of state and local tax services In this client-facing role, you will work closely with our Private Wealth practice and other tax professionals to advise high net worth individuals, families, business owners, executives, and family offices on complex state and local income tax matters, with a particular emphasis on residency and domicile planning, residency changes, and state tax controversy.

You will serve as a trusted advisor to clients consulting on individual, trust, and estate tax matters. As well as contemplating or implementing changes in residency, helping them understand the tax implications, documentation requirements, and practical considerations associated with establishing or terminating residency in a particular state. You will also represent and assist clients in residency audits and other individual income tax controversies before state taxing authorities.

This is a client-facing consulting role with a strong focus on technical advice, responsiveness, relationship management, and collaboration with Baker Tilly's Private Wealth practice.


Must be located in California near a Baker Tilly office.

What you’ll do:

  • Serve as a trusted advisor to high-net-worth individuals on state residency and domicile matters, including evaluating potential residency changes, understanding clients’ personal and financial circumstances, developing strategies to establish, maintain, or terminate residency, and advising on related tax implications and documentation requirements.
  • Help lead state residency and individual income tax audits and controversies, including responding to information document requests, developing factual and technical positions, preparing correspondence and protests, interacting and negotiating with state taxing authorities, and assisting with administrative appeals.
  • Advise clients on multistate individual income tax matters, including income sourcing, compensation, liquidity events, business transactions, asset sales, and credits for taxes paid to other jurisdictions.
  • Serve as an accessible SALT resource to Baker Tilly's Private Wealth practice and coordinate with federal, estate and gift, trust, business tax, and other specialists to provide timely, integrated advice.
  • Research complex state tax issues, monitor relevant legislative and regulatory developments, and contribute to technical memoranda, client communications, articles, presentations, webinars, and other thought leadership.
  • Contribute to business development by identifying opportunities, developing client and referral relationships, supporting proposals and presentations, and collaborating across Baker Tilly on prospective opportunities.
  • Maintain active communication with clients, manage expectations, and demonstrate a high degree of responsiveness and commitment to exceptional client service.
  • Help manage multiple consulting and controversy engagements, including project scope, staffing, scheduling, budgets, billings, collections, deadlines, and engagement economics.
  • Review and coach associates, providing timely technical feedback and supporting their professional development through Baker Tilly's Care and Teach philosophy

Minimum Qualifications

  • 4- year degree
  • 3 years of professional experience
  • License eligible for CPA, CMI, Law License/JD.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance or related field required; Masters or advanced degree preferred.
  • Three (3)+ year(s) experience in state and local tax, individual taxation, tax controversy, or a related area; professional services firm experience preferred.
  • Experience advising high-net-worth individuals, business owners, executives, family offices, or similar private clients strongly preferred.
  • Strong working knowledge of state individual income tax principles, particularly residency and domicile, statutory residency, income sourcing, and credits for taxes paid to other states.
  • Experience with state tax audits and controversy matters, particularly residency or individual income tax examinations, is strongly preferred.
  • Strong analytical, research, written, and verbal communication skills, with the judgment, discretion, responsiveness, and interpersonal skills necessary to advise high-net-worth clients and their advisors on complex and sensitive matters.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively across State & Local Tax, Private Wealth, and other specialty tax and advisory practices while leading teams and managing multiple consulting and controversy engagements, competing priorities, and deadlines.
  • Experience reviewing the work of associates and/or senior associates and providing coaching and technical guidance.
  • Eligibility to work in the U.S., without sponsorship, required.

Baker Tilly offers a comprehensive compensation and benefits package to eligible employees.


In California: pay rate range is $92,170 to $163,400

No jewelry may be worn on the jobsite except for medical ID jewelry and body piercings covered by appropriate clothing. Your Role

As a Cash Application Specialist, you'll play a critical role in supporting the financial health of the organization by ensuring customer payments are accurately applied and reconciled. Your attention to detail, analytical mindset, and commitment to accuracy help keep our accounts receivable processes running smoothly while supporting strong cash flow and exceptional customer service.

What You'll Do

  • Accurately apply customer payments received through checks, ACH, wire transfers, lockbox services, and credit card transactions.

  • Reconcile daily cash receipts to customer accounts and general ledger entries to ensure accurate financial reporting.

  • Research and resolve payment discrepancies, including short pays, overpayments, unapplied cash, and misapplied payments.

  • Post customer payments timely and accurately while maintaining the integrity of accounts receivable records.

  • Communicate with customers and internal teams to resolve payment-related questions and discrepancies.

  • Monitor and maintain unapplied cash balances, ensuring payments are allocated appropriately.

  • Generate and review reports related to cash applications, aging accounts, and payment activity.

  • Support month-end closing activities through reconciliations and cash application reporting.

  • Maintain accurate documentation and records within accounting and ERP systems.

  • Identify opportunities to improve processes, increase efficiency, and support automation initiatives.

  • Ensure compliance with company policies, accounting principles, and internal controls.

  • At Coastal, we win as a team. Once your assigned work is complete, you'll jump in to support your teammates and assist with other accounting and administrative needs as directed by your supervisor.

  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What You'll Bring

  • Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or related field preferred, or equivalent relevant experience.

  • Previous experience in cash application, accounts receivable, banking operations, or a related accounting role.

  • Strong understanding of cash application processes and accounts receivable functions.

  • Proficiency with ERP systems, accounting software, and Microsoft Excel.

  • Excellent attention to detail and ability to identify and resolve discrepancies.

  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills.

  • Effective communication skills and ability to collaborate across departments.

  • Ability to prioritize tasks and manage deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

  • Experience with high-volume transaction processing is a plus.

Why Join Coastal?

At Coastal, every team member makes a difference. As a Cash Application Specialist, you'll help strengthen the financial foundation of a growing organization by ensuring customer payments are processed accurately and efficiently.

  • Paid Time Off & Holidays

  • Employee Referral Program

  • Career Growth & Advancement Opportunities

  • Professional Development Opportunities

  • Collaborative Team Environment

  • Stable, Growing Company

description:

Continue growing with our family.

Management Level:

Class 1

Applicants must have no disciplinary actions within the last 6 months, a point level </= 6 attendance points and 6 months in current area unless the TM is promoting, then less than 6 months in current area is allowable.

Location: Bear Hollow Farm, Pineville, MO

Schedule: Monday through Friday from 5:50 am – 1:45 pm. Work schedule is subject to change based upon production needs.

Position Summary:

· This position is responsible for the daily care of flocks in growing houses by performing all essential duties. Other duties may be assigned.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

· Prepare houses for bird placement by installing metal & wire partitions to form accurate sized pens for bird placement as instructed, setup feed system, and safely operate truck/trailer to transfer birds from FCR to Growout and place in assigned pens (15%)

· Provide daily care of flock by properly calculating and recording feed amounts using calculator to determine # of pounds per pen, using hopper scale to weigh proper # of pounds per pen, distributing feed into feed hoppers by carrying buckets, monitoring flock for signs of injury/illness/slow growth and placing in recovery pen or euthanizing according to animal welfare policy, and collecting, recording wing band, and disposing of flock mortality, and administer and record medications via the water system as directed by management (30%)

· Maintains flock environment by flushing water lines weekly by turning flush valve, maintaining pen bedding to animal welfare standards, using handheld electric blower to clear dust from equipment (fans, inlets, etc.) once a week, and verifying feed/water/environmental control systems working properly and report any issues for correction (15%)

· Collect data regarding bird growth and development by analyzing fleshing (breast size) and sorting as needed, using digital scales to obtain average weight of each pen by weighing 60 females/30 males weekly, collecting weekly lab samples by using boot swabs for environment and cleft pallet swabs for birds, and assisting with euthanasia of birds designated by FCR out list as instructed by manager (30%)

Other duties, responsibilities, and activities:

· Other duties, responsibilities and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice. Such as: maintain vehicle by checking fluid levels, filters, tire pressure, and clean/disinfect to remove debris, operate a high pressure and regular water hose, maintains foot pans and hand sanitizer, maintains a clean and organized work/break area. (10%)

Biosecurity/Animal Welfare Requirements:

· The jobsite is a biosecure environment which requires showering, changing clothing and footwear before entering the facility. Appropriate clothing and footwear are provided by the Company. No jewelry may be worn on the jobsite except for medical ID jewelry and body piercings covered by appropriate clothing. Must be willing to sign an agreement to avoid any avian species (chickens, ducks, birds, etc.). Must be willing to sign and abide by the Company Biosecurity and Company Animal Welfare Guidelines.

Physical Demands and Work Environment:

· Physical: Must use safe lifting techniques. Must regularly lift and carry feed weighing up to 30 pounds and will occasionally be required to lift and carry bundles of shavings weighing up to 12 pounds. Will occasionally be required to pull/push 500 to 1000 pounds (wheeled carts). While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand majority of shift (concrete floor); walk; sit; use hands to handle or feel objects, tools, or controls; reach with hands and arms; balance; climb ladder; stoop/bend; talk or hear. Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision; distance vision; color vision; peripheral vision; depth perception; and the ability to adjust focus.

· Tools and Equipment: Must be able to use hand tools such as pitchfork, broom, hammer, chain breaker, pliers, screwdrivers, come-a-long, wire cutters; safe operation of vehicle to and from work area

· Environment: Required to work in dimly lit area on wet, slippery surfaces and in hot, dry, dusty, wet, and cold environments.

· Personal Protective Equipment Required: Safety goggles and/or glasses, face shield, chemical gloves, waterproof apron, and rubber boots are required when handling disinfectants. Must wear company provided facial covering. Ear plugs may be used as needed. NIOSH approved N95 particulate respirators may be worn as needed.

· Chemicals Commonly Used: Disinfectants, cleaners, lubricants, spray foam, vehicle fluids.

· Safety: Team member is expected to follow all applicable safety policies and procedures. These include but are not limited to Hazard Communication, Respiratory Protection, LOTO and Personal Protective Equipment. Team member is expected to identify, address and mitigate safety related risks.

· Mask policy will be in accordance with any local, state, or federal requirements but will be provided to any Team Member wishing to wear a mask.

  • Insemination of hens. This is a process where 1 team member inverts the hens’ oviducts and another team member places semen into the oviduct. Management and leads will inspect this process to insure correct placement of semen and insure correct hen handling methods are being used. Team members are required to rotate between the inverting job and semen placement job. Hens will be inspected for evidence of production during this process. (75%)
  • Collect semen free of containments from males. Semen collection duties will be assisted by management and leads based on team members ability to collect containment free semen without causing injury to the male. Visually inspecting semen and recording the quality scores . (5%)
  • Weighing of males and recording of weights and adjusting males’ feed. (5%)
  • Assisting management, management support and leads in the evulation of semen using microscope/densimeter and other equipment to determine semen quality. Males not having acceptable semen quality will be replaced. (5%)
  • Duties may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice, such as: washing/disinfecting vehicles; set up and cleaning of AI equipment; sanitizing AI breakroom; trimming beaks/vents; properly euthanizing selected or weak/ill birds in accordance with company policy (10%)

Accurately and efficiently selects Gordon Food Service (GFS) products for customer orders. Following designated pick lists and paths, selects items from the correct warehouse location (selection slots), properly labels, and places cases on pallets, or in designated areas for shipping, depending on type of warehouse.   • Work directly with plant technical personnel and machine OEMs to design the connectivity plan — including hands-on evaluation of PLC architecture, network topology, and data availability at the machine. (Technical / PLC background and technical communication)
  • Personally configure, test, and troubleshoot connectivity — protocol setup, PLC data mapping, and network integration — stepping in as the technical resource when plant or contractor capability falls short. (Hands-on technical execution)
  • Work with plant leadership, technical personnel, integrators, contractors, and corporate finance on cost estimates, project plans/timelines, and CIR building. (Communication and project management)
  • Drive execution across all teams and personnel involved to ensure each project delivers on schedule and at cost. (Project management)
  • Manage 10–20 projects simultaneously. (Multi-project program management)

REQUIREMENTS

Education: Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or another technical field preferred. Equivalent work experience is acceptable if the individual demonstrates hands-on technical ability to execute connectivity work directly, communication skills to lead the program, and project management capability.


Experience: 5+ years working with plant processes and equipment, including direct, hands-on experience configuring and troubleshooting machine connectivity — not solely oversight or coordination of others performing the work.


Technical Skills: Strong, hands-on knowledge of machine PLCs and industrial connectivity/networking (e.g., OPC-UA, MQTT, Ethernet/IP, or comparable protocols). Proficient in Microsoft Office. Background in Ignition and Anaplan a plus.


Communication Skills: Strong verbal and written communication. Demonstrated ability to translate technical information for non-technical stakeholders and vice versa.


Special Skills: Builds rapport quickly with plant teams and develops strong long-term relationships. Performs the technical work personally when needed, rather than relying solely on others to execute. Thrives in ambiguity and operates as a self-starter.


Travel: 25%

description:

Job Description:

You have the passion; we have the opportunities – let’s make a difference for Nebraskans!

Strong communication, organization, and customer service skills are important for this role. Bilingual skills in English and Spanish are strongly preferred to help serve a high number of Spanish-speaking clients. Rate for Bilingual is $1.75 above normal rate.

The Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) is seeking compassionate and committed individuals to join our team as Child and Family Services Specialists (CFSS). These professionals provide essential support to children and families through trauma-informed case management and advocacy. This work has traditionally been known as Child Protective Services. This vital role directly supports our mission of Helping People Live Better Lives.

About the Role
This role can be both challenging and deeply rewarding. As a CFSS, you will support families involved with the child welfare system, primarily due to concerns of abuse and/or neglect. You will assess safety, work collaboratively with families and community partners, and promote permanency and well-being for children. You will frequently travel to and meet with families in their homes, attend community meetings, participate in multidisciplinary team discussions, and be involved in legal proceedings, including providing court testimony when necessary.

Trainee starts at $22.327 with an increase to $26.183 after successful completion of training. Helping People Live Better Lives. Rate for Bilingual/Spanish position is $1.75 above normal rate.


Check out this video to learn more! https://youtu.be/XPwQ5CIDdhw

Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as a case manager for families referred to DHHS.
  • Assist families with Bilingual Spanish skills in the area.
  • Conduct home visits and comprehensive safety assessments in diverse community settings.
  • Advocate for the well-being of children and families while respecting cultural and individual diversity.
  • Apply family-centered practices and actively involve families in decision-making.
  • Collaborate with the legal system and other partners to support case permanency goals.
  • Utilize Structured Decision Making (SDM) tools to inform safety planning and case decisions.
  • Write timely, accurate, and professional documentation for internal and legal use.
  • Connect families to formal services and informal supports based on assessed needs.
  • Promote normalcy and permanency for children in care.
  • Apply trauma-informed and least-restrictive approaches to strengthen family functioning and resilience.

Work Schedule & Flexibility

The training schedule is generally Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. During this period, occasional after-hours field experiences and case-related responsibilities may be required. Following the completion of training, flexible work hours are available. Evening hours may be necessary to accommodate the needs of assigned families. This position also requires participation in an on-call rotation, which includes weeknights, weekends, and holidays.

Work Environment & Expectations

As a CFSS, you will sometimes enter homes that are in poor or unsanitary conditions and may encounter emotionally difficult situations. Worker safety is a top priority, and training and protocols are in place to prepare and support staff in the field.

You must be able to engage effectively with children and adults from diverse backgrounds, including those experiencing crisis, trauma, or instability. In some situations, you may be required to care for children temporarily while coordinating their transition to safe and appropriate placements.

While the work can be demanding, you will always have support. Ongoing supervision, training, peer support, and collaboration with law enforcement and legal partners help ensure both staff safety and effective outcomes for families. Even when you are in the field on your own, assistance is just a phone call away.

Watching the Realistic Job Preview video is highly recommended prior to applying.
It provides a candid look at the day-to-day responsibilities, challenges, and rewards of the Child and Family Services Specialist role. Viewing the video can help you make a more informed decision about whether this position is the right fit for your skills, interests, and long-term goals. Watch the video here. https://youtu.be/XPwQ5CIDdhw

Why Join Us?

Working at DHHS offers more than a paycheck—it provides purpose. Benefits include:

  • Vacation and sick leave begin accruing immediately upon hire.
  • 13 paid holidays.
  • Agency-backed retirement plan with employer match.
  • Supportive leadership and team culture.
  • Numerous opportunities for internal advancement and promotion.


Start your career with Nebraska today and make a meaningful impact on families across our state!


Requirements/Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications: A bachelor’s degree in social work, psychology, sociology, counseling, human development, mental health care, education, criminal justice, or other related fields. Consideration will be given to applicants who are enrolled in the final semester of their bachelor’s degree. Promotion to a Child and Family Services Specialist is contingent on successfully completing degree requirements and required training.

Preferred Qualifications: Bilingual Experience. Experience in child welfare, juvenile justice and/or case management experience, internships with human services/child welfare agencies will also be considered

Other: Valid Driver's license is required

description:

You’ll work alongside passionate bright minds. We offer a broad range of opportunities for those eager to build tomorrow’s world.

description:
For more than 70 years, MasterBrand has been shaping the places where people come together, enriching lives and creating meaningful memories for our customers. We are the #1 manufacturer of residential cabinets in North America, and our associates produce the most comprehensive portfolio of superior cabinetry products for the kitchen, bath and other parts of the home. Come see why our associates love working at MasterBrand.



Job Description:

This position plays a key role in advancing MasterBrand’s Global Ethics & Compliance program, Always Accountable, through the analysis, administration, and continuous improvement of compliance processes, risk management activities, regulatory reporting, third-party risk management, supply chain compliance, compliance risk assessments, audits, surveys, and data privacy activities. The Compliance Specialist will work collaboratively with internal business partners, customers, and suppliers to support compliance with regulatory requirements, compliance program monitoring and reporting, implementation of program initiatives, and continuous improvement activities.


The preferred work arrangement for this role is hybrid, with the position based in either Beachwood, Ohio, or Jasper, Indiana. Fully remote candidates may also be considered.

Responsibilities:

  • Evaluate and coordinate product compliance reporting to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Environmental and Climate Change Canada (ECCC), and state environmental regulators.
  • Develop, assess, and enhance data-driven compliance monitoring and reporting capabilities, including the use of analytics, automation, and artificial intelligence tools to identify trends, assess risks, improve program effectiveness, and support decision-making.
  • Use and evaluate Compliance technology tools, including Dow Jones screening tools, NAVEX EthicsPoint, Navex Disclosures, ASSENT, and related tools to manage compliance program initiatives.
  • Analyze and make recommendations regarding new and existing supplier compliance as part of MasterBrand’s Third-Party Risk Management Program, including performing due diligence, onboarding, sanctions screening, supplier compliance monitoring and audits, and related activities.
  • Coordinate Conflict Minerals reporting and related compliance activities.
  • Work closely with Sourcing and Supply Chain on Lacey Act, Toxic Control Substances Act (TSCA) and Code of Conduct supply chain reviews and related compliance activities.
  • Conduct and support global compliance risk assessments, benchmarking, and program maturity assessments.
  • Coordinate and assess program audits and reporting, wood surveys, sustainability surveys, customer survey responses, and related response strategies.
  • Evaluate and coordinate program improvements regarding multi-state data privacy compliance, including analyzing consumer deletion requests and similar requests made under state privacy laws.

Qualifications:

  • Associate’s degree required.
  • Direct experience in compliance, supply chain compliance, product compliance, third-party risk management, or a related function preferred.
  • Hands-on experience with compliance technology tools, reporting processes, due diligence platforms, or data analytics tools preferred.
  • Practical experience with artificial intelligence tools in a work environment, including but not limited to Microsoft CoPilot, preferred.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills, including the ability to work effectively with stakeholders across functions and levels of the organization.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and operate effectively in a fast-paced environment.
  • Excellent attention to detail and accuracy, particularly with data, reporting, and documentation.
  • Proven ability to maintain a high degree of confidentiality and exercise sound judgment.
  • Strong understanding of compliance processes, internal controls, risk management principles, and related terminology.
  • Strong proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Teams, and Outlook required.
  • Experience with dashboards or reporting tools preferred but not required.
  • Occasional travel may be required.

title: Full Stack Software Engineer, Manufacturing Systems
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

FULL STACK SOFTWARE ENGINEER, MANUFACTURING SYSTEMS

The application software team is the central nervous system of SpaceX – we create mission critical applications that are used throughout SpaceX to accelerate launch vehicle production and flight as well as systems that allow Starlink to grow into a worldwide fast, reliable Internet service. We are looking for engineers who treat fellow teammates with fairness, respect, and support.

Our team is currently creating and evolving systems to enable rapid build and reuse of Starship as well as designing the next generation manufacturing software that will be used in high throughput factories for Starlink. Other applications range from platforms that support concurrent streams of data from many always-on assets to manage the world’s largest satellite constellation to public facing systems where customers can join our Starlink network globally. We work closely with engineers throughout the company to create and update our systems with respect to crewed launches, Starship flights, changes to the Starlink network and much more.

Aerospace experience is not required to be successful here - rather we look for smart, motivated, respectful, collaborative engineers who love solving problems and want to make an impact on a super inspiring mission. You will have full ownership of challenging problems, working with a team of enthusiastic engineers with diverse perspectives to design and produce solutions that enable SpaceX to move towards our goals at a rapid pace. The success of the missions at SpaceX depends on the software that you and your team produce.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Develop highly reliable software solutions that are used across SpaceX
  • Create new applications that improve how SpaceX operates
  • Build prototypes to prove out key design concepts and quantify technical constraints
  • Own all aspects of software engineering and product development

  • Bring your voice to the table in team collaborations on architecture, design, and code reviews

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, math, or scientific discipline; OR 2+ years of professional experience building software in lieu of a degree
  • Experience in full stack development

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Programming experience in Python, C#.NET, Go, Scala, Java, or similar object-oriented language
  • 1+ years of rigorous experience building single page web applications
  • Experience with version control, continuous integration, and continuous delivery concepts
  • Expertise in designing software systems
  • Deep understanding of testing, continuous integration, build, deployment & monitoring
  • Expertise in profiling and improving application performance
  • Experience with build systems (Make, Bazel/Pants/Buck, Gradle) and package management tools (pip, npm)
  • Experience with UNIX-like operating systems and tools like Terraform, Ansible, Puppet for managing them
  • Experience working with in-stream data processing using Apache Kafka, RabbitMQ, ActiveMQ, or similar technologies
  • Production experience with Docker and Kubernetes
  • Front-end experience in Angular, React, or similar JavaScript framework
  • Database experience with PostgreSQL, SQL Server, or similar database technologies

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed
  • This role requires you to be onsite. Remote and/or hybrid work will not be considered

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

  • To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Head, Infrastructure and Operation
description:
The West Kowloon Cultural District Authority welcomes exceptional talent with a passion to realise the vision and mission of making the West Kowloon Cultural District a prime local and international destination for arts, culture and entertainment.

The Head, Infrastructure and Operation is responsible for defining, leading and continuously enhancing the Authority's enterprise technology infrastructure, operational platforms, cloud services, infrastructure cybersecurity operations, audio visual service delivery, and technology service management capabilities.


The role provides strategic leadership and operational accountability across the Authority's technology infrastructure landscape, ensuring technology platforms are cybersecure, resilient, scalable, cost-effective and future ready to support the Authority's business, venue, corporate and district-wide operations.


Working closely with business stakeholders, project teams, technology partners and service providers, this role establishes and maintains the technology infrastructure, operational standards, governance compliance, resilience capabilities and service management practices required to support the planning, design, construction and operation of WKCD IT facilities and services.


The role is accountable for supporting the Enterprise Architecture team on establishing technology infrastructure strategy, operational excellence, cybersecurity resilience, vendor governance, technology lifecycle management and IT service delivery performance, ensuring that infrastructure services remain aligned with the Authority's business objectives, technology roadmap and long-term development strategy.

You will be responsible for:

Technology Infrastructure Strategy and Governance

  • developing and executing the Authority's infrastructure and technology operations strategy, roadmap, architecture principles, standards and governance framework;
  • leading the planning, design, implementation, operation and continual improvement of enterprise technology infrastructure, including campus and venue networks; telecommunications and unified communications; data centre and cloud platforms; identity and access management services; infrastructure applications and shared technology services; and technology infrastructure supporting venue, operational and district-wide services;
  • establishing and maintaining technology standards, operational policies, service governance frameworks and lifecycle management processes to ensure secure, efficient and sustainable operations; and
  • providing strategic advice and recommendations to senior management on infrastructure strategy, technology investment, operational risks, resilience and emerging technologies.

Infrastructure and Technology Operations

  • overseeing the day-to-day operation of the Authority's infrastructure environment, ensuring high levels of service availability, reliability, performance and operational efficiency;
  • managing hybrid infrastructure environments, including on-premises, private cloud and public cloud services, ensuring appropriate governance, performance, cybersecurity and cost optimization;
  • leading infrastructure modernisation initiatives, including technology refresh, automation, cloud adoption, standardisation and operational improvement programmes;
  • driving the adoption of infrastructure automation, proactive monitoring, observability and analytics to improve service quality and operational effectiveness; and
  • overseeing capacity management, performance monitoring and technology lifecycle planning to ensure infrastructure services support current and future business requirements.

Cybersecurity Operations and Operational Resilience

  • leading infrastructure cybersecurity tools delivery and operations, ensuring appropriate controls are implemented to protect systems, services, information assets and technology platforms against cybersecurity threats;
  • overseeing vulnerability management, infrastructure hardening, cybersecurity monitoring, privileged access management and incident response coordination in collaboration with relevant cybersecurity functions;
  • ensuring disaster recovery, backup, business continuity and service recovery capabilities are established, maintained and regularly tested;
  • leading operational resilience initiatives and ensuring critical infrastructure services meet recovery objectives and business continuity requirements; and
  • maintaining oversight of infrastructure-related risks, audit findings, compliance obligations and remediation activities.

Service Delivery and Operational Excellence

  • establishing, monitoring and continuously improving service management processes, operational procedures, service levels and performance metrics;
  • ensuring infrastructure services are delivered in accordance with agreed service level targets, cybersecurity requirements, operational standards and business expectations;
  • leading major incident management and post-incident reviews to identify root causes and drive service improvements;
  • ensuring technology services are operationally ready before production deployment through effective service transition, documentation, monitoring and support arrangements; and
  • driving continuous improvement programmes to improve reliability, customer experience, operational efficiency and service quality.

Financial, Procurement and Vendor Management

  • developing and managing infrastructure and operations budgets, including capital expenditure and operational expenditure planning;
  • leading procurement, tendering, evaluation and contract management activities relating to infrastructure, cloud, telecommunications, cybersecurity and managed services;
  • establishing effective vendor governance mechanisms to ensure suppliers meet contractual, operational, cybersecurity and performance obligations;
  • driving technology cost optimisation, asset lifecycle management and value-for-money initiatives across the infrastructure portfolio; and
  • developing and maintaining strategic relationships with technology partners, service providers and industry stakeholders.

Leadership and People Management

  • building, leading and developing a high-performing infrastructure and technology operations team;
  • fostering a culture of service excellence, accountability, innovation, collaboration and continuous improvement;
  • leading workforce planning, succession planning, capability development and knowledge management activities to ensure long-term organisational capability;
  • monitoring industry developments, emerging technologies, keeping abreast of comparable statutory bodies’ infrastructure development references and best practices, recommending innovations and improvements where appropriate; and
  • performing any other duties from time to time as reasonably assigned by the Authority.

You should:

  • possess a recognised university degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems or a related discipline. A postgraduate qualification is an advantage. Master’s degree on relevant discipline is a big plus;
  • have at least 15 years of relevant IT experience, including substantial experience in senior infrastructure, operations or technology leadership role within a large and complex organisation, including governmental or statutory bodies;
  • demonstrate proven experience leading enterprise-scale infrastructure, cloud services, technology operations and service delivery functions, preferably for mission-critical operations, venue technologies, large-scale public facilities, property developments, cultural institutions, transport, hospitality or similar operational environments;
  • have strong experience in technology strategy formulation, infrastructure architecture, operational governance and technology transformation;
  • possess sound knowledge of hybrid cloud platforms; enterprise networking and telecommunications; infrastructure architecture and operations; identity and access management; cybersecurity principles and controls; disaster recovery and business continuity; Audio Visual service delivery and operations; and IT Service Management frameworks;
  • demonstrate successful delivery of major infrastructure, cloud migration, operational transformation or technology modernisation initiatives;
  • possess strong financial management, procurement, contract negotiation and vendor governance experience;
  • demonstrate excellent leadership, stakeholder engagement, communication and influencing skills;
  • have proven experience building, developing and managing multidisciplinary technical teams.
  • be proficient in written and spoken English and Chinese;
  • preferably have professional certifications in IT infrastructure, networking, systems administration, or cloud technologies, such as CCNA, CCNP, MCTS, MCSA, MCSE, Microsoft Azure, AWS, or equivalent qualifications; and
  • preferably have recognized governance, service management, project delivery, or agile certifications, such as ITIL, COBIT, PMP, PMI-ACP, Agile PM, PRINCE2, or equivalent.

title: Senior Full Stack Engineer - South Bank, QLD
description:
Senior Full Stack Engineer - South Bank, QLD

Job no: 532742

Brand: Product and Technology

Work type: Full time

Location: Queensland

Categories: Digital and Technology

At Flight Centre Travel Group (FCTG) our purpose is to 'open up the world for those who want to see'. Every day, we give people all around the world the opportunity to experience something amazing, travel!

We're looking for a Senior Full Stack Engineer to help us build and scale a travel platform relied on by some of Australia's largest corporate operators. It's a full stack role for someone who genuinely enjoys the hard problems: complex, high availability systems that process high volume travel booking at scale, end to end, from backend services through to the interfaces people rely on every day.

You’ll be a key technical contributor on capabilities that matter, the kind of work that shapes how thousands of travellers experience booking, changing, and managing their trips. You won't be maintaining someone else's legacy code in isolation; you'll be designing and building new capability from the ground up, including change and cancellation support, waitlist management, and deep policy engine integration, then owning it end to end in production. This is a chance to make decisions that stick: the architecture you choose, the standards you set, and the patterns you introduce will shape how the platform evolves for years to come.

Day to day:

Core Backend Development

  • Design, build, and own complex backend services and APIs using C# / .NET (ASP.NET Core), with a strong focus on reliability, performance, and correctness
  • Deliver new modules including: change and cancellation processing, waitlist capability, and policy engine integration across the travel platform
  • Implement and consume RESTful APIs and SOAP/Web Services that integrate with airline GDS systems, internal booking engines, and third party travel platforms
  • Build robust, fault tolerant service components capable of handling high volume, time critical travel booking

Frontend Development

  • Design and build responsive, accessible user interfaces in React that give travel bookers and administrators a clear, reliable view into complex processes
  • Own end to end feature delivery: from API design through to the React components and state management that consume them
  • Work with component libraries and design systems to keep the UI consistent, maintainable, and easy to extend
  • Optimise frontend performance (load times, rendering, bundle size) for users working in time critical, high pressure booking scenarios

System Reliability & Observability

  • Ensure the platform maintains high uptime, this is a mission critical system for travel operations; downtime has direct operational impact
  • Instrument services with Datadog, including APM tracing, custom metrics, log correlation, and dashboard creation to provide full observability across the travel booking stack, frontend and backend
  • Define and monitor SLOs/SLIs, respond to incidents, and lead post incident reviews to drive continuous reliability improvement
  • Proactively identify and resolve performance bottlenecks, memory issues, and degradation patterns before they impact customers

Architecture & Technical Leadership

  • Lead technical design for new capabilities, producing clear architecture and API design documentation before implementation
  • Conduct rigorous code reviews and hold the team to high standards for API design, exception handling, test coverage, component quality, and service contract quality
  • Identify and reduce technical debt, particularly around legacy integration patterns, file based data exchange, and monolithic components
  • Mentor and support junior and mid level engineers, particularly on C# best practices, .NET internals, React patterns, and API design

DevOps & Delivery

  • Champion DevOps practices across the team: CI/CD pipeline ownership, automated testing (unit, integration, contract, and frontend), and deployment hygiene
  • Collaborate with platform and cloud engineering on Azure based infrastructure, ensuring services are containerised, scalable, and maintainable
  • Work closely with product managers, designers, and business stakeholders to translate complex travel booking requirements into clean, maintainable full stack solutions
  • Participate actively in agile delivery processes, sprint planning, refinement, retrospectives and drive continuous improvement

You will be perfect for the role if you have:

  • 7+ years of professional software engineering experience with deep, hands on expertise across both C# / .NET (.NET 6+, ideally .NET 8) and React, comfortable owning features end to end rather than favouring one side of the stack
  • Proficient with AI coding tools (Claude, GitHub Copilot) and able to critically evaluate AI generated code in production contexts
  • Expert level knowledge of the .NET ecosystem: ASP.NET Core, Entity Framework Core, .NET Identity, and integration frameworks such as MassTransit or NServiceBus
  • Expert level experience with React, including hooks, component driven architecture, state management, and building maintainable, well tested frontend applications
  • Strong track record designing and building complex REST APIs and Web Services (SOAP/WSDL); including versioning, contract design, and error handling at scale
  • Proven ability to instrument and operate production systems using Datadog: APM, dashboards, monitors, log pipelines, and AI powered anomaly detection and forecasting features
  • Experience with relational databases (SQL Server, PostgreSQL, or Sybase) including complex query optimisation and schema design

Highly Regarded

  • Experience in travel technology GDS systems (Amadeus, Sabre, Galileo), NDC, PNR management, travel platforms
  • Background in resource scheduling and logistics
  • Familiarity with API gateways, service mesh, microservices strategies
  • Azure cloud experience: App Services, AKS, Service Bus, Application Insights
  • Experience with design systems, component libraries, or accessibility (WCAG) standards

Tech Stack

  • .NET 6 / 8, ASP.NET Core, C#
  • React, JavaScript, HTML/CSS
  • REST APIs, SOAP / Web Services (WSDL), JSON, XML
  • Entity Framework Core, .NET Identity, MassTransit or NServiceBus
  • SQL Server, Sybase, SQL query optimisation
  • Datadog (APM, dashboards, monitors, log pipelines, SLOs)
  • Azure (App Services, AKS, Service Bus, Storage)
  • GitHub, Azure DevOps, Jenkins, automated CI/CD pipelines
  • xUnit / NUnit, Moq, Jest / React Testing Library, integration and contract testing

What you will enjoy:

  • Culture: you will be employed by an inclusive company that offers a team culture like no other in the industry - Flight Centre Travel Group Australia is proud to be a certified Great Place To Work® Australia New Zealand Pty Ltd
  • Our People: FCTG is an Equal Opportunity Employer and encourage all suitably qualified applicants to apply, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander People and people from racial, ethnic, or ethno-religious minority groups and people with disability
  • Development: Individualised Learning & Development pathway options
  • Access to 'LinkedIn Learning' for ongoing skills development: over 24,500 courses in over 20 languages
  • Exclusive Staff Discounts: Accessible via our employee-only portal with 350+ of Australia’s leading retailers, health and wellness discounts, financial planning advice, employee share plan and more
  • Travel Discounts: Including family and friends - flights, hotels, tours, cruises, travel insurance and more
  • Brightness of Future: Career opportunities in a network of brands and businesses across the globe - we promote from within
  • Corporate Health Discounts: Access exclusive discounts on health insurance plans for you and your family with our partner, BUPA, access to internal gym
  • Mental Health: Support and Employee Assistance Program for staff and family
  • Social: Regular awards nights, social team-building and industry events, with the opportunity to attend global conferences (Bangkok in 2026)

title: Microsoft Architect
description:
The Microsoft Architect is based in Chicago and is the Firm's senior technical authority on the Microsoft platform and is accountable for the architecture and evolution of Sidley's Microsoft estate. The role's first priority is a well-architected, governed, and consistently deployed productivity foundation (SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, Exchange Online and Outlook, the Microsoft 365 applications, Entra, Purview, Graph, and tenant administration) so that lawyers and staff can collaborate securely and client confidentiality is protected by design. On that foundation, the Architect leads Copilot enablement across the Firm, layers in the broader Microsoft AI platform (Foundry, Work IQ, Fabric IQ, Foundry IQ, and Microsoft Scout) as readiness allows, and partners directly with Microsoft engineering to maximize the return on the Firm's investment.

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Design and own the target-state architecture and standards for the Microsoft productivity estate, including SharePoint and OneDrive information architecture, permissions and sharing, lifecycle, and SharePoint Advanced Management to keep the estate Copilot-ready.
  • Architect Teams (including Teams Phone and Rooms), Exchange Online and Outlook, Microsoft 365 Groups, and the wider Microsoft 365 application portfolio, including data residency, Microsoft 365 Backup, and integration with the Firm's document management systems.
  • Lead enterprise deployment and remediation of the Microsoft stack, retiring inconsistent policies, oversharing, and legacy configuration through pilots, waves, and change management.
  • Configure Microsoft Entra and design the tenant's administrative architecture: the Microsoft 365 permission model, admin roles, tenant-wide policies and configuration profiles, and configuration-as-code baselines.
  • Establish, with Information Security and Information Governance, the Microsoft Purview architecture (sensitivity labels, data loss prevention, retention, information barriers, eDiscovery, and legal hold) and the interfaces to Intune, Defender XDR, and Entra.
  • Drive Copilot enablement across the estate (readiness and data hygiene, licensing, grounding, connectors, and adoption guardrails), operate the Copilot Control System, and establish the agent identity and governance model (Entra Agent ID, Microsoft Agent 365, and Copilot Studio).
  • Architect Microsoft Foundry and its integration with the Azure estate, define governance for Fabric, Power BI, and the Power Platform, and translate Microsoft's AI and productivity roadmap (Work IQ, Fabric IQ, Foundry IQ, and Microsoft Scout) into Firm priorities, pilots, and licensing inputs.
  • Liaise with Microsoft engineering as the Firm's primary technical counterpart, bringing requirements and escalations to Microsoft; partner with Security, Enterprise IT Services, Network, Endpoint, and business stakeholders; and mentor Microsoft 365 administrators and engineers.

Education and/or Experience:

Required:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • A minimum of 7 years architecting or administering Microsoft 365 in an enterprise environment.
  • Deep understanding of SharePoint Online and OneDrive, and enterprise-level expertise in Microsoft Copilot, Teams, Exchange Online and Outlook, and the Microsoft 365 productivity applications.
  • Deep knowledge of the Microsoft 365 permission model, policies, and configuration profiles, with proficiency in the Microsoft 365 admin center, the Copilot Control System, and the workload admin centers.
  • Foundational understanding of Microsoft Entra and the ability to configure Entra and other Azure-based services; working knowledge of Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Graph, Intune, and the Power Platform.
  • Ability to architect Microsoft Foundry within an Azure estate, with a base understanding of Work IQ, Fabric IQ, and Foundry IQ and current awareness of Microsoft's AI roadmap, including Microsoft Scout.
  • Demonstrated experience partnering directly with Microsoft engineering or product teams, and the ability to produce clear architecture documentation for technical and non-technical audiences.

Preferred:

Job Details

Birnbaum, MD, Quality Leadership Award, Medina Hospital is known for its excellence in delivering safe, patient-centered care that is timely, effective, efficient, and equitable. Medina Hospital has also been recognized for its commitment to creating a positive environment that empowers and engages staff by the American Nurses Credentialing Center. Here, you can build a rewarding, lifelong career while receiving endless support and encouragement.

As Nuclear Medicine Technologist, you will utilize the latest medical equipment and technology to attain functional images, prepare and administer radiopharmaceuticals, and perform various non-imaging studies as necessary. In addition to working with complex apparatus, you will also spend a substantial amount of time interacting directly with both in- and outpatients, providing injections and scans. This role offers an excellent way to enhance your current skillsets, gain extensive hands-on experience and make a difference in the lives of patients every day.

A PRN (as needed) caregiver in this position works days + on-call, 7:00am—5:00pm.

A caregiver who excels in this role will:

  • Perform elution of 99mTc generators, prepare radiopharmaceuticals and ensure compliance with regulations and recommendations by state/federal regulatory and accreditation agencies.
  • Perform hot lab responsibilities, such as elution of generator according to prescribed procedure and manufacturer specifications using aseptic technique.
  • Perform elute quality control using aseptic technique.
  • Perform radiopharmaceuticals kit preparations and quality control according to departmental procedure and manufacturer specifications using aseptic techniques.
  • Label and record required documentation according to department procedures.
  • Administer radiopharmaceuticals according to department protocol using aseptic technique in compliance with state/federal regulations and accreditation agencies.
  • Ascertain correct patient, study and radiopharmaceuticals by checking patient ID, requisitions and radiopharmaceuticals label prior to radiopharmaceutical administration.
  • Properly record pharmaceuticals.
  • Educate patients regarding procedures, equipment and exams to ensure understanding and cooperation.
  • Ensure patient safety during and after exams.
  • Assist with scheduling patients as needed.
  • Perform venipuncture as necessary and maintain competencies.
  • Perform quality control and assurance procedures.
  • Perform daily, weekly, quarterly and annual procedures on dose calibrators, scintillation well counter and thyroid probes, and scintillation cameras.
  • Identify, document and report sub-optimum results to supervisor.
  • Adhere to Department of Health, TJC, and department regulations governing performance of above procedures.
  • Maintain required record keeping and documentation for all diagnostic and therapeutic procedures.
  • Acquire, archive, transmit and print images via PACS.
  • Complete after-hours transmission of images and appropriate paperwork.
  • Process billing via RIS.
  • Perform nuclear imaging/counting procedures according to department protocols and computer acquisition and analysis.

Minimum qualifications for the ideal future caregiver include:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Nuclear Medicine or graduate of a two-year accredited school in an Allied Health Program or certification from a CAHEA approved Nuclear Medicine Technologist Training Program
  • Registered Technologist credentialed by the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists [R.T(N) (ARRT)] in good standing OR Certified Nuclear Medicine Technologist (CNMT) through the Nuclear Medicine Technology Certification Board
  • Current state licensure (RL)
  • Basic Life Support (BLS) certification through the American Heart Association (AHA) or the American Red Cross

Preferred qualifications for the ideal future caregiver include:

  • One year of experience as a Nuclear Medicine Technologist.


Physical Requirements:

  • Requires standing and walking for extended periods of time.
  • Must be able to lift or assist with lifting patients of varying weight and manipulate equipment daily.
  • Requires exposure to radioactive material.

Personal Protective Equipment:

  • Follows standard precautions using personal protective equipment as required.

Cleveland Clinic Health System administers an influenza prevention program. You will be required to comply with this program, which will include obtaining an influenza vaccination on an annual basis or obtaining an approved exemption.

Job Description:

Entegris Leadership Development Program


Jump start your Global Supply Chain Career at Entegris. Our Entegris Leadership Development Program (ELDP) is uniquely designed to provide new to market and entry-level professionals meaningful exposure to the core supply chain disciplines that drive our business. The ELDP specifically targets candidates with a balanced mix of high technical acumen, hunger for professional development and the capacity to complete complex work projects while participating in the company’s custom learning curriculum.

ELDP seeks to advance the development of talented supply chain professionals through the completion of three 12-month assignments in the areas of Supply Planning, Procurement, and Logistics. Inclusion in this program will provide exposure to high-level company mentors, active learning events with senior leaders and challenging project work that directly contributes to key corporate and divisional objectives. Culminating in a permanent job placement within the ranks of Entegris, this program seeks to accelerate the process of identifying and positioning high-potential future leaders of Entegris.


Rapidly build upon your technical capabilities:

title: Quality Control Project Manager
description:
Corporate Overview

Argonaut Manufacturing Services Inc. is a leading contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) specializing in aseptic fill-finish services for pharmaceutical and biopharmaceutical products. Headquartered in Carlsbad, California, Argonaut supports clients from clinical development through commercial manufacturing, with a focus on product quality, yield optimization, and reliable delivery.

Argonaut provides flexible drug product manufacturing solutions, including vial, syringe, and cartridge filling, as well as combination filling capabilities. The company also offers analytical services and short-term cGMP storage to support clients throughout the manufacturing process.

With a commitment to quality standards and hands-on client support, Argonaut works closely with customers to help ensure consistent, compliant, and efficient manufacturing while meeting critical timelines and patient needs.

Benefits and Pay Range

Benefits for this position, subject to applicable eligibility requirements.

  • Medical Insurance

  • Dental Insurance

  • Vision Insurance

  • Company Paid Life Insurance 1X annual Salary

  • Voluntary Life Insurance

  • Long-Term Disability Insurance and Short-Term Disability Insurance

  • Flexible Spending Account and Health Saving Account

  • 401(K) Retirement Plan

  • 10 Days of Paid Time Off

  • 10 Paid Holidays Annually

The pay range for this position is between $117K - $128K annually. Factors which may affect starting pay within this range may include geography/market, skills, education, experience, and other qualifications of the successful candidate.

Position and Scope

The QC Project Manager leads and coordinates Quality Control projects and programs from initiation through completion, ensuring alignment with business objectives, customer expectations, regulatory requirements, timelines, and financial goals. The role serves as a key cross-functional liaison between QC, QA, Program Management, Finance, customers, and external partners, providing project leadership, risk and resource management, issue resolution, and performance oversight.

This role is 100% On-Site, Monday – Friday 8 hours/day (excluding lunch break). Overtime, weekends and holidays may be required. Flexible start time between 6:00am and 9:00am with a consistent schedule. Exceptions to the schedule must be approved by the manager in advance.

Responsibilities and Duties

  • Lead end-to-end QC project management for complex pharmaceutical and biopharmaceutical programs, including project scope, timelines, milestones, resources, risks, deliverables, testing priorities, and customer commitments.
  • Serve as the primary QC project lead, coordinating activities across QC, QA, Project Management, Finance, customers, and external laboratory partners to ensure timely, compliant, and efficient execution.
  • Translate customer requirements into executable testing strategies, project plans, resource requirements, regulatory deliverables, and compliance objectives.
  • Manage stability programs from study initiation through testing, data review, reporting, and completion, ensuring adherence to protocols, schedules, SOPs, quality requirements, and customer commitments.
  • Ensure QC testing readiness across personnel, equipment, analytical methods, documentation, and laboratory systems, while proactively identifying and resolving operational risks and resource constraints.
  • Participate in root cause investigations, CAPAs, change controls, remediation efforts, and continuous improvement initiatives to strengthen quality, compliance, and operational efficiency.
  • Utilize project metrics to monitor performance, identify trends and resource gaps, and provide data-driven insights to support project and business decisions.
  • Partner with Finance to track project activities and billable work, assign costs to appropriate customer and GL accounts, support accurate invoicing, and reconcile financial activity with approved project scope.
  • Manage project governance and executive communications, including status reporting, risks, milestones, resource and financial updates, escalations, and key decisions.
  • Participate in effective customer and stakeholder relationships through clear communication, alignment on requirements and deliverables, and timely resolution of project issues.

Listed responsibilities are an essential, but not exhaustive list, of the usual duties associated with the position. Changes to individual responsibilities may occur due to business needs.

Requirements and Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in chemistry, biochemistry, biology, pharmaceutical sciences, or a related scientific discipline.
  • 5+ years of experience in pharmaceutical, biopharmaceutical, or other GMP-regulated environments, including Quality Control experience.
  • 3+ years of experience in QC project management, laboratory operations, stability management, or related project leadership.
  • Demonstrated experience managing multiple concurrent projects and cross-functional teams in a regulated environment.
  • Strong working knowledge of GMP, QC laboratory operations, stability programs, analytical testing, data integrity, and quality systems.
  • Experience with project planning, scheduling, risk management, resource coordination, and customer deliverables.
  • Experience with deviations, investigations, CAPAs, change controls, and audit/inspection readiness.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office; experience with Power BI or similar reporting tools preferred.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and effectively engage senior leadership and customers.

title: Senior Engineer, Customer Access Studies
description:
The Alberta Electric System Operator (AESO) is responsible for the safe, reliable, and economic planning and operation of the Alberta Interconnected Electric System. We provide open and non-discriminatory access to Alberta’s interconnected power grid and also facilitate Alberta’s competitive wholesale electricity market. The AESO strives to foster an inclusive, diverse and equitable workplace where people feel respected and welcomed for who they are, together we deliver high performance and innovative results.

Job Description

The AESO is the sole provider of system access service on Alberta's transmission system, and the Customer Grid Access team plays a critical role in fulfilling this mandate. Through the AESO's Connection Process, the Customer Access Studies (CAS) team performs and reviews project interconnection engineering studies that support the reliable integration of new generation, load, and transmission-connected projects into Alberta's power system.

Reporting to the Manager, Customer Access Studies, the Senior Engineer is responsible for running interconnection engineering studies and developing engineering solutions to project challenges that support customer connection projects. You will provide technical decision-making, engineering assessments, documentation, and technical regulatory support to facilitate System Access Service Requests to the AIES. Working closely with internal and external stakeholders, you will contribute to technical deliverables, support project execution through the AESO Connection Process, and provide guidance to Engineers and Engineers-in-Training.

What You'll Do

  • Prepare Engineering Study Scope documents for projects within the assigned Cluster (regional area) in collaboration with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Conduct power flow, stability, and short circuit studies, as well as advanced power system analysis studies for project interconnection using PSS/E software.
  • Determine options or alternative solutions for connecting Market Participants to the Alberta transmission network and justify the preferred alternative based on technical, economic, and impact factors.
  • Prepare and review Single Line diagrams, Engineering Connection Assessments, Connection Proposals, and supporting documentation for connection projects.
  • Review and accept Distribution Deficiency Reports and analyze system constraints identified through engineering studies.
  • Collaborate with AESO Operations, Planning, Markets, Project Engineering, Grid Analytics, and Standards & Modeling teams to develop mitigation plans, forecasts, and models that support customer access studies and connection projects.
  • Maintain technical project documentation and effective communication with Market Participants to resolve technical issues.
  • Provide technical leadership, engineering expertise, and support for customer connection projects through the AESO Connection Process.

What You’ll Bring to Us

  • B.Sc. in Electrical Engineering; a post-graduate degree in Electrical Power Systems is considered an asset.
  • Registered with or eligible for registration with APEGA (P.Eng.).
  • Approximately 8-10 years of engineering experience in the electric utility industry, including at least five years of exposure to power systems and distribution planning or operations.
  • Proficiency in PSS/E software and Python.
  • Experience conducting power flow, stability, and short circuit studies, as well as advanced power system analysis.
  • Strong understanding of transmission and distribution system planning, customer interconnections, and utility operations.
  • Distribution system planning and detailed design expertise is considered an asset.

Why Join AESO

  • Help shape the future of Alberta's electricity system.
  • Lead complex, high-impact customer interconnection projects.
  • Work with industry-leading engineers and technical experts.
  • Influence major transmission infrastructure and system planning decisions.
  • Grow your career in a collaborative environment that values innovation, technical excellence, and continuous learning.

What We Offer

This full-time opportunity offers a competitive salary, paid vacation and flex time, health and dental benefits, mental health support, a defined contribution pension plan, and learning and development opportunities as part of your overall compensation package. We support a hybrid work environment, where the team is in the office on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays. Mondays and Fridays are flexible for where you work best.

You'll Thrive in This Role If

  • You enjoy solving complex power system and customer interconnection challenges through technical analysis and sound engineering judgment.
  • You are energized by conducting power flow, stability, short circuit, and advanced power system studies to support critical grid access decisions.
  • You can balance technical detail, project priorities, and stakeholder needs to deliver practical engineering solutions.
  • You thrive in a collaborative environment and enjoy working with internal teams, Market Participants, Transmission Facility Owners, Distribution Facility Owners, and consultants.
  • You are confident leading technical discussions and communicating complex engineering concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • You take a proactive approach to identifying system constraints, evaluating alternatives, and recommending solutions that support reliable system operation.
  • You enjoy mentoring Engineers and Engineers-in-Training and sharing your expertise to support team development.
  • You are motivated by work that directly impacts Alberta's evolving electricity system and supports the reliable integration of new generation, load, and transmission-connected projects.

Application deadline: October 11, 2026
